status: Checked TimeDelta unit constructors, integer accessors and canonical std Duration conversions; public panic adapters, general arithmetic, production integration and whole-product qualification remain separate.

compiler.bootstrap: Explicit Python B0, followed by native HIA B1, B2, B3 and component compilation.

entry.signature: u64 f0(const u8* source, u64 source_len, u8* output, u64 output_capacity, u8* workspace, u64 workspace_len)
entry.status_encoding: Core u32 zero extended to u64 by the fixed native borrowed-buffer wrapper.

caller_preconditions: Advertised source and output ranges are live for the synchronous call, readable for source and writable for output.
Source and output ranges do not overlap, including exact aliasing. Source is not concurrently modified.
No alignment is required. Lengths are actual allocated capacities; invalid pointers or invented capacities are outside the contract.
Zero-length workspace is never read or written. Native retains no pointers and has no mutable global state.

source.byte_order: eight little-endian u64 words; signed arguments use two's-complement bits

fields.name: operation
fields.meaning: 0: canonical TimeDelta::new; 1: weeks; 2: days; 3: hours; 4: minutes; 5: seconds; 6: milliseconds; 7: microseconds; 8: nanoseconds; 9: canonical std Duration to TimeDelta; 10: zero

fields.name: argument
fields.meaning: signed canonical seconds for 0; signed value in selected unit for 1..8; unsigned canonical std Duration seconds for 9; required zero for 10

fields.name: nanoseconds
fields.meaning: u64 nanoseconds for 0 and 9; required zero for other operations

source.mutation: Never modified; all eight words are loaded before any output write.

output.byte_order: 21 little-endian u64 words; signed results use two's-complement bits

fields.name: valid
fields.value: 1 when the actual original constructor succeeds; otherwise 0

fields.name: canonical_nanoseconds
fields.value: canonical nonnegative fraction below one billion

fields.name: num_microseconds
fields.value: signed original optional value or zero

fields.name: num_nanoseconds
fields.value: signed original optional value or zero

fields.name: std_seconds
fields.value: unsigned original standard duration seconds or zero

fields.name: std_nanoseconds
fields.value: unsigned original standard duration fraction or zero

fields.name: is_zero
fields.value: 1 exactly when original is_zero() is true

output.absent: A failed constructor writes version 1 followed by twenty zero words. Optional accessor failure leaves the valid duration and other accessor values intact.
output.tail: Bytes after offset 168 remain unchanged. Frame and capacity errors leave the entire output unchanged.

semantics.canonical_duration: Match TimeDelta::new: seconds from -9223372036854776 through 9223372036854775, fraction below one billion; lower endpoint fraction at least 193000000, upper endpoint at most 807000000. Wider-than-u32 nanoseconds are explicitly rejected by the observer's transport guard.
semantics.large_units: Checked weeks/days/hours/minutes/seconds constructors use integer seconds. Bound arguments symmetrically by floor(9223372036854775 / unit factor) before multiplication. This preserves the original checked multiplication and TimeDelta::new result for all i64 inputs.
semantics.small_units: Milliseconds rejects i64::MIN, preserving the original symmetric duration limit. Microsecond and nanosecond constructors accept all i64 values. Use quotient and remainder directly, adjusting negative remainder to Euclidean form without an overflowing floor-quotient reconstruction.
semantics.integer_accessors: Use the exact original truncated num_seconds and signed subsec_nanos rules for negative canonical fractions. Weeks follows num_days()/7; days/hours/minutes use truncating integer division. Milliseconds remains representable across the complete constructor range.
semantics.optional_accessors: Preserve original checked whole-second multiplication followed by checked fraction addition, including cases where a mathematically combined expression could be evaluated differently. Guard multiply and use sign-specific addition bounds before executing checked arithmetic.
semantics.standard_duration: Input operation 9 represents an already canonical std::time::Duration: unsigned seconds and fraction below one billion. Noncanonical fractions are rejected as semantic transport values before constructing the original standard type. Original from_std rejects values above TimeDelta::MAX. Original to_std rejects negative canonical seconds, including negative subsecond durations.
semantics.scope: Checked unit constructors and integer/std accessors only. Public panicking constructor adapters, floating accessors, arbitrary TimeDelta checked_mul/div/add/sub, timezone conversion, production integration and whole-product gates are separate.

status_precedence.condition: output capacity is below 168, before reading source or validating workspace

source size is not 64, workspace is nonempty, version is not 1, operation is outside 0..10, any reserved word is nonzero, nanoseconds is nonzero for operations other than 0 or 9, or operation 10 has a nonzero argument
valid frame; exactly 168 output bytes encode the actual original constructor and accessor observations, or version 1 followed by zero words for a failed constructor

differential_corpus.coverage: Canonical duration endpoints and invalid fractions; exact optional total microsecond/nanosecond boundaries; full i64 power-of-two neighborhoods and extremes; all checked unit boundaries; deterministic full-range and valid-range inputs; unsigned standard-duration overflow and canonical fraction guards; actual TimeDelta::zero.
differential_corpus.controls: Two fills and exact/excess output capacities for every semantic case. All 168 shorter output capacities and three nonempty workspace sizes for all eleven operations; truncated/oversized source, invalid metadata, nonzero reserved/unused words and nonzero zero-constructor arguments. All inputs, outputs, tails and unaligned guards compared.
differential_corpus.recording: Complete input, original output and native-call transcript retained as gzip streams, with SHA-256 hashes of every uncompressed byte.
